# The soak judge's fixtures

Soak outputs written by hand, one for each thing the judge (ADR 0215,
`tests/Varve.Benchmarks/SoakJudge.cs`) must say. The pipeline's
`soak-judge-fixtures` job runs `--soak-judge-fixtures` on this directory on
every build, so the gate's failure path is proven, not assumed. A fixture's
name is its expected verdict:

| Prefix | Exit | Fixtures |
|---|---:|---|
| `holds-` | 0 | `flat`: the working set within a few MB of a flat line, the dataset steady from minute 25; `loaded`: the dataset filled before the clock (the load of ADR 0215 point 1, amended 2026-11-02) and steady from the first sample; `collector-headroom`: every fifth sample the collector commits 40 MB it does not use, and the working set rises with it; `shrinking`: the working set falls by a sixth from minute 30 to the end; `windows-trimmed`: four hours on Windows, private bytes on a line of 50 bytes a commit with the collector's bursts above it and the working set trimmed below it |
| `misses-` | 1 | `slope`: the working set on a line of 80 bytes a commit, 60 allowed; `hourly-leak`: 45 bytes a commit and 4 MB more at the top of every hour, which the fit measures as 76; `band`: one sample far off the line; `committed`: the collector's committed memory climbs past twice the live heap and 128 MB, the working set flat; `handles`: handles climbing past their bound; `derived`: `derived/` files climbing past theirs |
| `cannot-` | 2 | `growing`: the dataset grows for the whole run; `drifting`: filled before the clock and steady until minute 40, then growing to 8% over its median, out of the ±5% the gate judges in; `short`: forty minutes, less than the steady state and twenty minutes more; `collector`: the server collector, not the shipped one |

The judge fits the process's memory against commits from minute 30: the
working set where the soak ran on Linux, private bytes on Windows (ADR 0215,
amended 2026-11-03). Its slope is at most 60 bytes a commit and every sample
lies within ±25% of the fit's intercept, widened by the collector's unused
memory at that sample.

Each is a sample every half minute in the soak's own columns
(`Soak.Header`), after the lines the soak prints before its table: the
collector it ran under, the OS (`# os linux` or `# os windows`, from
2026-11-03), its handles before the dataset opened and, from 2026-11-02, what
the load before the clock brought the dataset to. The fixtures before
2026-11-03 keep the `own MB` column the soak then wrote, which the judge no
longer reads; the bounds are the ones `SoakBounds` gives the fixtures'
commits and quads. The three new fixtures of 2026-11-03 were generated by a short
script from the shapes their rows say, with a fixed seed per sample.
